concept.title: Chebotarev's theorem that every square submatrix of the `p × p` DFT matrix
concept.concept_description:
Chebotarev's theorem that every square submatrix of the `p × p` DFT matrix
is nonsingular, which in turn follows from a resultant/Vandermonde computation over `Q(ζ_p)`
using the irreducibility of the `p`-th cyclotomic polynomial — machinery that Mathlib already
contains (`Polynomial.cyclotomic_irreducible`, `IsPrimitiveRoot`).

concept.title: Compression Research B6: Compression ↔ one-way functions (the cryptography link)
concept.concept_description:
**Part of:** Research plan — *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound* (Phase B, Question 2: can random number generators help?).

## Research question
Worst-case short-program-finding is **provably hard under standard assumptions**: roughly, if you could always find a short description for every `x` quickly, you could invert one-way functions. Compression ⇋ computational hardness.

## Approach
- State precisely **which compression tasks are equivalent to inverting OWFs** (distinguishable / polynomial-time Kolmogorov complexity literature).
- Derive what that implies for achievable worst-case bounds.

## Deliverable
A precise characterization mapping compression tasks to cryptographic assumptions.

## Purpose
Calibrates the whole plan: **randomness helps compression exactly up to the computational-hardness boundary, and no further.** Converts the intuition "randomness should help" into a quantified expectation.

**Milestone:** M8 (theory, 3–6 weeks).

concept.title: Compression Research B5: PRNG-generated real-world data — detection and seed recovery
concept.concept_description:
**Part of:** Research plan — *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound* (Phase B, Question 2: can random number generators help?).

## Research question
A surprising amount of real-world data **is** PRNG output: game worlds, simulations, certain file formats, crypto keys. Detect it and recover the seed → compress to ~0 bits beyond the seed.

## Approach
- Robust **PRNG fingerprinting**: which generator family produced this stream?
- **Seed recovery**: Berlekamp–Massey for LFSRs; solver-based inversion for other families.
- A classifier that routes each file to *seed-compressible* vs. *model-compressible*.

## Deliverable
Detection + seed-recovery tooling and a benchmark of seed-compressible files found in real corpora.

## Falsifiability / gate
For a recovered seed: decompressed output must exactly reproduce the file. Measures what fraction of real data is seed-compressible.

**Milestone:** M2 (cheap, warm-up infrastructure). Related: [[B1]].

concept.title: Compression Research B3: Almost-lossless / Monte Carlo compression
concept.concept_description:
**Part of:** Research plan — *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound* (Phase B, Question 2: can random number generators help?).

## Research question
Pigeonhole governs *exact* decoding for *all* strings. Relax to: **decoder fails with probability ≤ ε** (almost-lossless). Random codebooks (Shannon's random-coding argument) then reach near-optimal rates — the counting bound relaxes by an ε-dependent factor.

## Approach
- Constructive almost-lossless schemes with small failure probability.
- The real obstacle is **decoder search complexity** (naive random coding is exponential), not the rate — tackle that.
- Error detection (checksums) so failures are **never silent**.

## Deliverable
A scheme plus a proof that decode succeeds with probability ≥ 1−ε, and its exact decoding complexity.

## Falsifiability / gate
For each scheme: bound on P(failure) and an explicit decoder-complexity figure. No silent corruption allowed.

**Milestone:** M9.

concept.title: Compression Research A1: Price of universality — minimax redundancy of universal decompressors
concept.concept_description:
**Part of:** Research plan — *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound* (Phase A, Question 1: separating the decompressor from the data).

## Research question
One shared decompressor `U` must serve all inputs. A decompressor specialized to a *class* of data does better per class. What is the **price of universality** — the minimax redundancy a universal scheme must pay over a per-distribution scheme?

## Approach
- Derive closed-form / tight bounds on universal redundancy for natural source classes: stationary sources, finite-state, Markov.
- Express redundancy as a function of message length `n` and class complexity.

## Deliverable
Rigorous bounds on universal vs. per-distribution redundancy, and a conclusion on whether specialized decompressors are theoretically worth pursuing.

## Falsifiability / gate
Bounds must match or beat known minimax rates from the literature (Rissanen-style redundancy). If specialization doesn't move bits from *message* to *shared*, the direction is dead.

**Milestone:** M5 (theory, ~2 weeks).

# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — after the Jacobi-signed Weil floor

The formal results in `Catalog/Tropical/JacobiSigned*.lean` settle the JACSIGN
experiment: the Jacobi-signed circle count `W(N) = ∑_{x²+y²=1} (x/N)` is
multiplicative (`circleWeightZ_mul`), vanishes identically when a factor is
`≡ 3 (mod 4)` (`WZ_semiprime_eq_zero_of_three_mod_four`), is not a residue dial
(`not_residue_dial_prime`, `not_residue_dial_modulus`), and is pinned at the Weil
floor by an *exact identity* — `A(1)² + A(ν)² = 4p` (`jacobsthal_identity`) — whose two
legs are the Gaussian coordinates of `p` (`two_squares_odd_leg`).  The following
conjectures are the natural next cycle.

---

## C1. Every character-weighted circle count is a quadratic-twist trace, hence at the floor

**Conjecture.** Let `ψ` be any nontrivial multiplicative character mod `p` of order `d`
and set `W_ψ(p) = ∑_{x²+y²=1} ψ(x)`.  Then `|W_ψ(p)| ≤ (d) √p`, and `W_ψ(p)` is a
`ℤ[ζ_d]`-linear combination of traces of Frobenius of the curves `y² = x³ - c x`
(`d = 2`) or of Jacobi sums `J(ψ, χ)` in general; in particular no choice of `ψ`
escapes the square-root floor.

*The key insight is* that summing `y` away turns any circle weight into
`∑_x ψ(x)(1 + χ(1-x²))`, i.e. a **Jacobi sum**, and Jacobi sums have absolute value
exactly `√p` — so the floor is a property of the circle, not of the weight.

*Why now?* The second-moment machinery in `JacobiSignedWeilFloorBound.lean`
(`chiSum_quadratic`, `moment`, `sum_sq_comp`) is character-agnostic; Mathlib already has
`jacobiSum` with `jacobiSum_mul_jacobiSum_inv`, so the `√p` step is within reach.

---

## C2. The two-leg trade-off is a hard obstruction to factor leakage

**Conjecture.** For semiprimes `N = pq` the pair `(W(N), A_ν(N))` is equidistributed on
the "Weil circle" `u² + v² ≤ 16N` in the sense that, for any fixed `ε > 0`, the map
`N ↦ W(N)/(4√N)` has limiting distribution the (Sato–Tate-type) pushforward of the
product of two arcsine laws — hence carries `O(1)` bits about `p` versus `q`.

*The key insight is* that `jacobsthal_identity` forces `W(p)` and its nonresidue twin to
trade off with `4p` conserved: any large signal in one leg is compensated in the other,
so a witness reading only one leg sees a conserved-quantity projection, never the split.

*Why now?* The identity is now a theorem, so the statement is unconditional in its
algebraic half; only the equidistribution half is open, and the `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`
vanishing already proves a density-1/2 zero-information family.

---

## C3. `v₂(W(N))` is a complete obstruction to a "dial + parity" witness

**Conjecture.** For `N = pq` with both primes `≡ 1 (mod 4)`, `v₂(W(N)) = 2` exactly, and
more generally `v₂(W(N)) = #{primes p | N with p ≡ 1 mod 4}`; consequently the 2-adic
valuation of the statistic counts the number of `1 mod 4` prime factors — a genuine but
*already publicly computable* invariant (it is determined by `N mod 4` for semiprimes),
so it leaks nothing new.

*The key insight is* that `W_mod_four` gives `v₂ = 1` at each `1 mod 4` prime and
multiplicativity adds valuations, so the 2-adic content of the statistic is exactly the
count of such factors and nothing more.

*Why now?* `W_mod_four` and `WZ_mul` are proved; the conjecture is a short corollary for
semiprimes and an induction for general `N`, and its "leaks nothing new" half is a
precise, falsifiable information claim.

---

## C4. Weil-floor attainment has positive density

**Conjecture.** For every `ε > 0` the set of primes `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)` with
`W(p)² > (1-ε)·4p` has positive relative density; equivalently, the odd leg `a` of
`p = a² + b²` satisfies `b = O(p^{ε})` for a positive-density set of primes.

*The key insight is* that near-attainment means `p = a² + b²` with `b` tiny, i.e. `p`
lies just above a square — so the conjecture is a statement about primes of the form
`a² + b²` with `b` bounded, closely tied to Landau–Ramanujan and to primes represented by
thin quadratic families.

*Why now?* `weil_floor_near_attained` proves attainment at 97.7 % for `p = 173`;
`jacobsthal_identity` converts the analytic question into a purely Diophantine one about
the two-square decomposition, where sieve technology applies.

---

## C5. No polynomial-time-computable circle statistic beats the floor

**Conjecture.** Let `S(N)` be any statistic of the form `∑_{(x,y) ∈ C(N)} w(x, y)` with
`w` a product of Jacobi-type characters and `C(N)` a conic mod `N`.  Then `S` is
multiplicative in the modulus, `|S(N)| = O(N^{1/2+o(1)})`, and `S(N)` is computable from
`N` alone in time `N^{1+o(1)}` but from `(p,q)` in time `polylog(N)` — so the
"free-witness" gap is exactly the Weil floor.

*The key insight is* that the CRT proof of `circleWeightZ_mul` never used the specific
weight: multiplicativity plus a per-prime Weil bound is automatic for any character
weight on any conic, which is why CIRC, BQF, GSP and JACSIGN all die the same death.

*Why now?* `circleWeightZ_mul` is proved for an arbitrary modulus and the per-prime bound
is proved by an elementary second moment; generalising both to arbitrary conics and
character products is a mechanical extension of the existing Lean development.

namespace PrimeUncertainty

variable {p : ℕ}

/-- Tao's additive uncertainty principle, as a property of the modulus `p`. -/
def SumUncertainty (p : ℕ) [NeZero p] : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ZMod p → ℂ, f ≠ 0 → p + 1 ≤ (supp f).card + (supp (dftZMod f)).card

/-- Chebotarev's property: every square submatrix `(ω^{s t})_{s ∈ S, t ∈ T}` of the DFT matrix
of `ZMod p`, indexed by injective families `S` and `T`, is nonsingular. -/
def ChebotarevProperty (p : ℕ) [NeZero p] : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (S T : Fin n → ZMod p), Function.Injective S → Function.Injective T →
    (Matrix.of fun j k : Fin n => ez (S j * T k)).det ≠ 0

section General

/-- The *local* form of the reduction: if all minors of the size `|supp f|` are nonsingular,
then `f` obeys the additive bound. -/
theorem sum_bound_of_chebotarev_at (f : ZMod p → ℂ) (hf : f ≠ 0)
    (H : ∀ S T : Fin (supp f).card → ZMod p, Function.Injective S → Function.Injective T →
      (Matrix.of fun j k : Fin (supp f).card => ez (S j * T k)).det ≠ 0) :
    p + 1 ≤ (supp f).card + (supp (dftZMod f)).card := by

  by_contra hcon
  push_neg at hcon
  set A : Finset (ZMod p) := supp f with hA
  set Zs : Finset (ZMod p) := Finset.univ.filter (fun k : ZMod p => dftZMod f k = 0) with hZs
  have hpart : Zs.card + (supp (dftZMod f)).card = p := card_zeroSet_add_card_supp f
  have hAne : A.Nonempty := by
    rcases Function.ne_iff.1 hf with ⟨x, hx⟩
    exact ⟨x, mem_supp.2 (by simpa using hx)⟩
  have hnle : A.card ≤ Zs.card := by omega
  obtain ⟨T', hT'sub, hT'card⟩ := Finset.exists_subset_card_eq hnle
  -- enumerate the support and the chosen part of the zero set
  set TA : Fin A.card → ZMod p := fun k => (A.equivFin.symm k : ZMod p) with hTA
  set TZ : Fin A.card → ZMod p :=
    fun j => (T'.equivFin.symm (Fin.cast hT'card.symm j) : ZMod p) with hTZ
  have hTAmem : ∀ k, TA k ∈ A := fun k => (A.equivFin.symm k).2
  have hTZmem : ∀ j, TZ j ∈ T' := fun j => (T'.equivFin.symm _).2
  have hTAinj : Function.Injective TA := by
    intro a b hab
    have : A.equivFin.symm a = A.equivFin.symm b := Subtype.ext hab
    simpa using congrArg A.equivFin this
  have hTZinj : Function.Injective TZ := by
    intro a b hab
    have h1 : T'.equivFin.symm (Fin.cast hT'card.symm a)
        = T'.equivFin.symm (Fin.cast hT'card.symm b) := Subtype.ext hab
    have h2 := congrArg T'.equivFin h1
    simp only [Equiv.apply_symm_apply] at h2
    exact Fin.cast_injective _ h2
  have hSinj : Function.Injective (fun j => -(TZ j)) := fun a b hab => hTZinj (neg_injective hab)
  -- the kernel vector
  set v : Fin A.card → ℂ := fun k => f (TA k) with hv
  have hvne : v ≠ 0 := by
    have hk : Nonempty (Fin A.card) := ⟨⟨0, Finset.card_pos.2 hAne⟩⟩
    obtain ⟨k⟩ := hk
    intro h0
    have : v k = 0 := by rw [h0]; rfl
    exact (mem_supp.1 (hTAmem k)) this
  set M : Matrix (Fin A.card) (Fin A.card) ℂ :=
    Matrix.of fun j k => ez ((fun j => -(TZ j)) j * TA k) with hM
  have hMv : M.mulVec v = 0 := by
    funext j
    have hsum : ∑ k : Fin A.card, ez (-(TZ j) * TA k) * f (TA k)
        = ∑ x ∈ A, ez (-(TZ j * x)) * f x := by
      have h1 : ∑ k : Fin A.card, ez (-(TZ j) * TA k) * f (TA k)
          = ∑ x : A, ez (-(TZ j) * (x : ZMod p)) * f (x : ZMod p) :=
        Fintype.sum_equiv A.equivFin.symm _ _ (fun k => rfl)

    rw [hsum, hfull, hz]

theorem sumUncertainty_of_chebotarev (H : ChebotarevProperty p) : SumUncertainty p :=

    intro k₀
    rw [hf]
    simp only

    · simp

    intro x hx
    by_contra hxr
    have hzero : f x = 0 := by

      intro x _ hx

        by_contra hne
        exact hx (hsupp (mem_supp.2 hne))
      simp [hfx]
    rw [hrestrict, Finset.sum_image (fun a _ b _ hab => hT hab)]
    have hval : ∀ k : Fin n, ez (-(-(S j) * T k)) * f (T k) = ez (S j * T k) * v k := by
      intro k
      rw [hfT k]
      congr 2
      ring
    simp_rw [hval]
    have := congrFun hMv j
    simpa [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct] using this

  have hpart : Zs.card + (supp (dftZMod f)).card = p := card_zeroSet_add_card_supp f
  have hZcard : n ≤ Zs.card := by
    have hsub : Finset.image (fun j => -(S j)) Finset.univ ⊆ Zs := by
      intro x hx
      obtain ⟨j, _, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hx
      exact Finset.mem_filter.2 ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, hzero j⟩
    have hcard : (Finset.image (fun j => -(S j)) Finset.univ).card = n := by
      rw [Finset.card_image_of_injective _ (fun a b hab => hS (neg_injective hab))]
      simp
    calc n = (Finset.image (fun j => -(S j)) Finset.univ).card := hcard.symm
      _ ≤ Zs.card := Finset.card_le_card hsub
  have hAcard : (supp f).card ≤ n := by
    calc (supp f).card ≤ (Finset.image T Finset.univ).card := Finset.card_le_card hsupp
      _ ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).card := Finset.card_image_le
      _ = n := by simp
  have := H f hfne
  omega

/-- **The additive uncertainty principle is exactly Chebotarev's theorem.** -/
theorem chebotarev_iff_sumUncertainty : ChebotarevProperty p ↔ SumUncertainty p :=
  ⟨sumUncertainty_of_chebotarev, chebotarev_of_sumUncertainty⟩

/-- Chebotarev's property fails for the composite modulus `4`. -/

  intro H
  obtain ⟨f, hf, _, hlt⟩ := sum_bound_fails_zmod_four
  have := sumUncertainty_of_chebotarev H f hf
  omega

end General

/-! ## The unconditional half of Chebotarev: arithmetic progression minors -/

section Prime

variable [hp : Fact p.Prime]

/-- **Generalised Vandermonde minors.**  Any minor of the DFT matrix whose *rows* are indexed by
an arithmetic progression `a, a + d, …` with `d ≠ 0` is nonsingular, for arbitrary distinct
columns `T`.  This is the case of Chebotarev's theorem that the polynomial method settles
unconditionally. -/
theorem det_ne_zero_of_AP_rows {n : ℕ} (a d : ZMod p) (hd : d ≠ 0) (T : Fin n → ZMod p)
    (hT : Function.Injective T) :
    (Matrix.of fun j k : Fin n => ez ((a + ((j : ℕ) : ZMod p) * d) * T k)).det ≠ 0 := by
  classical
  set z : Fin n → ℂ := fun k => ez (d * T k) with hz
  set c : Fin n → ℂ := fun k => ez (a * T k) with hc
  have hzinj : Function.Injective z := by
    intro x y hxy
    exact hT (mul_left_cancel₀ hd (ez_injective hxy))
  have hfactor : (Matrix.of (fun j k : Fin n => ez ((a + ((j : ℕ) : ZMod p) * d) * T k)))
      = (Matrix.vandermonde z).transpose * Matrix.diagonal c := by
    ext j k
    rw [Matrix.mul_diagonal]
    simp only [Matrix.of_apply, Matrix.transpose_apply, Matrix.vandermonde_apply, hz, hc]
    have hsplit : (a + ((j : ℕ) : ZMod p) * d) * T k
        = a * T k + ((j : ℕ) : ZMod p) * (d * T k) := by ring
    rw [hsplit, ez_add, ez_natCast_mul]
    ring
  rw [hfactor, Matrix.det_mul, Matrix.det_transpose, Matrix.det_diagonal]
  refine mul_ne_zero (Matrix.det_vandermonde_ne_zero_iff.2 hzinj) ?_
  exact Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff.2 fun k _ => ez_ne_zero _

/-- The transposed statement: minors whose *columns* are indexed by an arithmetic progression
are nonsingular as well. -/
theorem det_ne_zero_of_AP_cols {n : ℕ} (a d : ZMod p) (hd : d ≠ 0) (S : Fin n → ZMod p)
    (hS : Function.Injective S) :
    (Matrix.of (fun j k : Fin n => ez (S j * (a + ((k : ℕ) : ZMod p) * d)))).det ≠ 0 := by
  have hEq : (Matrix.of (fun j k : Fin n => ez (S j * (a + ((k : ℕ) : ZMod p) * d)))).transpose
      = Matrix.of (fun j k : Fin n => ez ((a + ((j : ℕ) : ZMod p) * d) * S k)) := by
    ext j k
    simp only [Matrix.transpose_apply, Matrix.of_apply]
    congr 1
    ring
  rw [← Matrix.det_transpose, hEq]
  exact det_ne_zero_of_AP_rows a d hd S hS

end Prime

/-! ## The Fourier transform cannot vanish on a short arithmetic progression -/

/-- **Chebotarev in the arithmetic-progression case (analytic form).**
For `f ≠ 0` on `ZMod p` with `p` prime, the DFT `f̂` cannot vanish at all the points
`a, a + d, …, a + (n-1)d` of an arithmetic progression of length `n = |supp f|` and nonzero
common difference `d`.

theorem exists_dft_ne_zero_on_AP (f : ZMod p → ℂ) (hf : f ≠ 0) (a d : ZMod p) (hd : d ≠ 0) :

/-- **Additive uncertainty principle for supports of size at most two.**

* `PrimeUncertainty.det_ne_zero_of_card_le_two` : Chebotarev's nonsingularity for all minors
  of size at most two.
-/

import Mathlib
import Catalog.MachineLearning.PrimeUncertainty.Chebotarev

open Finset Polynomial FourierFA FourierCyclic
open scoped Real

namespace PrimeUncertainty

variable {p : ℕ}

/-! ## Comparing the two uncertainty inequalities -/

/-- **The additive bound implies the multiplicative one.**  If `a, b ≥ 1` and `a + b ≥ p + 1`
then `a * b ≥ p`; so Tao's inequality really is a strengthening of Donoho–Stark. -/
theorem product_bound_of_sum_bound {a b p : ℕ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 1 ≤ b)
    (hsum : p + 1 ≤ a + b) : p ≤ a * b := by
  obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le ha
  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hb
  nlinarith [Nat.zero_le (x * y)]

/-- Elementary AM–GM in `ℕ`: `4ab ≤ (a+b)²`. -/
theorem four_mul_le_add_sq (x y : ℕ) : 4 * (x * y) ≤ (x + y) ^ 2 := by
  rcases le_total x y with h | h
  · obtain ⟨t, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le h
    nlinarith [Nat.zero_le t]
  · obtain ⟨t, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le h
    nlinarith [Nat.zero_le t]

/-- What the multiplicative bound alone gives: `(|supp f| + |supp f̂|)² ≥ 4n`, i.e. the sum of
the support sizes is at least `2√n`.  This is `o(n)` and hence far weaker than `n + 1`. -/
theorem four_mul_le_sum_sq {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (f : ZMod n → ℂ) (hf : f ≠ 0) :
    4 * n ≤ ((supp f).card + (supp (dftZMod f)).card) ^ 2 := by
  have hprod := FourierCyclic.uncertainty_zmod f hf
  calc 4 * n ≤ 4 * ((supp f).card * (supp (dftZMod f)).card) := by omega
    _ ≤ ((supp f).card + (supp (dftZMod f)).card) ^ 2 := four_mul_le_add_sq _ _

/-! ## New regimes -/

section Prime

variable [hp : Fact p.Prime]

/-- **Dual small-spectrum case.**  If the spectrum of `f` has at most two points then the
additive bound holds. -/
theorem sum_bound_of_card_supp_dft_le_two (f : ZMod p → ℂ) (hf : f ≠ 0)
    (hcard : (supp (dftZMod f)).card ≤ 2) :
    p + 1 ≤ (supp f).card + (supp (dftZMod f)).card := by
  have hg := sum_bound_of_card_supp_le_two (dftZMod f) (dft_ne_zero f hf) hcard
  rw [card_supp_dft_dft f] at hg
  omega

/-- If the spectrum is a single point then `f` is (a multiple of) a character, so its support is
everything.  In particular the additive bound is attained. -/
theorem card_supp_eq_of_card_supp_dft_eq_one (f : ZMod p → ℂ) (hf : f ≠ 0)
    (hcard : (supp (dftZMod f)).card = 1) : (supp f).card = p := by
  have h := sum_bound_of_card_supp_dft_le_two f hf (by omega)
  have hle : (supp f).card ≤ p := by
    calc (supp f).card ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset (ZMod p)).card := Finset.card_le_card (subset_univ _)
      _ = p := card_univ_zmod
  omega

/-- **Master theorem.**  The additive uncertainty principle `|supp f| + |supp f̂| ≥ p + 1` is
established here in four regimes: small support, small spectrum, support an arithmetic
progression, spectrum an arithmetic progression. -/
theorem sum_bound_of_regime (f : ZMod p → ℂ) (hf : f ≠ 0)
    (h : (supp f).card ≤ 2 ∨ (supp (dftZMod f)).card ≤ 2 ∨
      (∃ a d : ZMod p, ∃ m : ℕ, d ≠ 0 ∧ m ≤ p ∧
        supp f = (range m).image (fun j : ℕ => a + (j : ZMod p) * d)) ∨
      (∃ a d : ZMod p, ∃ m : ℕ, d ≠ 0 ∧ m ≤ p ∧
        supp (dftZMod f) = (range m).image (fun j : ℕ => a + (j : ZMod p) * d))) :
    p + 1 ≤ (supp f).card + (supp (dftZMod f)).card := by
  rcases h with h | h | ⟨a, d, m, hd, hm, hAP⟩ | ⟨a, d, m, hd, hm, hAP⟩
  · exact sum_bound_of_card_supp_le_two f hf h
  · exact sum_bound_of_card_supp_dft_le_two f hf h
  · exact sum_bound_of_supp_eq_AP f hf a d hd m hm hAP
  · exact sum_bound_of_supp_dft_eq_AP f hf a d hd m hm hAP

/-! ## Chebotarev for small minors -/

/-- Every minor of the DFT matrix of size at most two is nonsingular. -/
theorem det_ne_zero_of_card_le_two {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ 2) (S T : Fin n → ZMod p)
    (hS : Function.Injective S) (hT : Function.Injective T) :
    (Matrix.of fun j k : Fin n => ez (S j * T k)).det ≠ 0 := by
  interval_cases n
  · simp
  · rw [Matrix.det_fin_one]
    exact ez_ne_zero _
  · have hne : S 1 ≠ S 0 := fun h => by
      have := hS h
      revert this
      decide
    have hd : S 1 - S 0 ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.2 hne
    have hEq : (Matrix.of fun j k : Fin 2 => ez (S j * T k))
        = (Matrix.of (fun j k : Fin 2 =>
            ez ((S 0 + ((j : ℕ) : ZMod p) * (S 1 - S 0)) * T k))) := by
      ext j k
      fin_cases j
      · norm_num
      · norm_num
    rw [hEq]
    exact det_ne_zero_of_AP_rows (S 0) (S 1 - S 0) hd T hT

end Prime

end PrimeUncertainty

indicator functions.

| `n`  | min sum | `n + 1` | additive bound holds? |
|------|---------|---------|-----------------------|
| 3    | 4       | 4       | yes (tight)           |
| 4    | **4**   | 5       | **no** (`A = {0,2}`)  |
| 5    | 6       | 6       | yes (tight)           |
| 6    | **5**   | 7       | **no**                |
| 7    | 8       | 8       | yes (tight)           |
| 8    | **6**   | 9       | **no**                |
| 9    | **6**   | 10      | **no**                |
| 11   | 12      | 12      | yes (tight)           |
| 12   | **7**   | 13      | **no**                |

(Dirac delta) and `|supp f| = n` (character) — both are formalised as
`sum_bound_sharp_delta` and `sum_bound_sharp_character`.

The composite witness `n = 4`, `A = {0, 2}` (an index-2 subgroup, `|supp f| = |supp f̂| = 2`)
is formalised as `sum_bound_fails_zmod_four`.

## 2. Chebotarev test: minimum modulus of a DFT minor

Minimum of `|det (ω^{st})_{s∈S,t∈T}|` over all pairs of equal-size subsets:

| `n`  | min |det| | attained at |
|------|--------------|-------------|
| 4    | 0            | `S = T = {0,2}` |
| 5    | 1.000        | — |
| 6    | 0            | `S = {0,2}, T = {0,3}` |
| 7    | 0.868        | `S = {1,3}, T = {2,5}` |
| 8    | 0            | `S = {0,2}, T = {0,4}` |
| 9    | 0            | `S = {0,3}, T = {0,3}` |
| 11   | 0.316        | `S = {2,5,6,9}, T = {1,4,7,10}` |

Consistent with `chebotarev_iff_sumUncertainty`: singular minors exist exactly for the
composite moduli, i.e. exactly where the additive bound fails.

## 3. The parity-weighted exponent criterion

For every pair `(S, T)` of `n`-subsets we computed the coefficients

`c_r = #{σ even : ∑_j s_j t_{σ(j)} ≡ r} − #{σ odd : …}`  (mod `p`).

* `p = 5, 7` and `n = 3`; `p = 7, 11, 13` and `n = 4`; `p = 11`, `n = 5`:
  **no** pair ever produced `c ≡ 0`, in agreement with Chebotarev's theorem and with
  `chebotarev_criterion`.
* For `n = 3` **every** pair admits a permutation whose exponent is realised uniquely
  (`0` failures out of `100` for `p=5` and `1225` for `p=7`).  This is exactly the mechanism
  used by the Lean proof `det_fin_three_ne_zero`.

`|supp f| · |supp f̂| ≥ p` allows `|supp f| = |supp f̂| = ⌈√p⌉`; e.g. for `p = 11` the pair

# Future directions — the additive uncertainty principle on `ZMod p`

State of the thread after this cycle (all statements below refer to
`Catalog/MachineLearning/PrimeUncertainty/`, all proofs are `sorry`-free):

* The multiplicative bound `|supp f| · |supp f̂| ≥ p` (`FourierCyclic.uncertainty_zmod`) is
  **strictly weaker** than the additive bound `|supp f| + |supp f̂| ≥ p + 1`
  (`product_bound_does_not_imply_sum_bound`), while the additive bound implies it
  (`product_bound_of_sum_bound`).  The product bound alone only gives `2√p`
  (`four_mul_le_sum_sq`).
* The additive bound is **equivalent** to Chebotarev's nonsingular-minor property
  (`chebotarev_iff_sumUncertainty`), and is equivalent to a finite combinatorial statement
  about parity-weighted permutation exponents (`chebotarev_criterion`).
* It is **proved** here when `|supp f| ≤ 3`, when `|supp f̂| ≤ 3`, when `|supp f| ≥ p − 3`,
  when `supp f` is an arithmetic progression, and when `supp f̂` is an arithmetic progression
  (collected in `sum_bound_known_regimes`).
* It **fails** for composite moduli (`sum_bound_fails_zmod_four`), and is **sharp** at both
  ends (`sum_bound_sharp_delta`, `sum_bound_sharp_character`).

The remaining open case is `4 ≤ |supp f| ≤ p − 4` with unstructured support and unstructured spectrum.  The following
conjectures are bold, falsifiable, and each is a concrete next cycle.

---

## Conjecture A (Parity-gap conjecture). For all `n ≥ 2`, all injective `S, T : Fin n → ZMod p`, the parity-weighted exponent counter `permCoeff S T` is nonzero somewhere; in fact `max_r |permCoeff S T r| ≥ 1` is attained at a residue of the form `∑_j S(σ j) T j` for a permutation `σ` of *minimal* Coxeter length among those realising its exponent.

**The key insight is** that `chebotarev_criterion` reduces an analytic nonvanishing statement
about roots of unity to a *counting* statement about `S_n` acting on `ZMod p`, so the whole
difficulty of Chebotarev's theorem is concentrated in the fibres of the map
`σ ↦ ∑_j S(σ j) T j` — and the numerical data show the fibres are never parity-balanced.

**Why now?** The criterion is already formalised and `det_ez_ne_zero_of_unique_perm` discharges
every configuration in which one fibre is a singleton, which covers `n ≤ 3` completely.  What
is missing is a combinatorial invariant distinguishing even from odd permutations inside a
fibre; the length statistic is the natural candidate and is finitely checkable for `n = 4`.

## Conjecture B (`(1−ω)`-adic valuation conjecture). Write `M(u) = det((1+u)^{s_j t_k}) ∈ ℤ[u]`. Then `ord_u M = n(n−1)/2` and the leading coefficient is `∏_{j<k}(s_k−s_j)(t_k−t_j) / ∏_{j<k}(k−j)`, an integer prime to `p`; consequently every DFT minor is nonsingular.

**The key insight is** that the exponent-`u` filtration of `ℤ[u]` refines the vanishing of the
minor modulo the prime `(1−ω)` of `ℤ[ω]`, converting Chebotarev's theorem into an identity
between a generalised Vandermonde determinant and a Weyl-type dimension formula.

**Why now?** All the surrounding infrastructure now exists in this development (primitive root
`om`, character `ez`, Leibniz expansion, cyclotomic minimal polynomial); the one missing
ingredient is the Schur-polynomial specialisation `s_λ(1,…,1) = ∏_{j<k}(t_k−t_j)/(k−j)`, which
Mathlib does not yet contain and which is a self-contained, reusable addition.

## Conjecture B′ (Odd-fibre conjecture). For all `n ≥ 2`, all primes `p > n` and all injective `S, T : Fin n → ZMod p`, some residue `r` is realised by an **odd** number of permutations `σ` with `∑_j S(σ j) T j = r`.

**The key insight is** that the parity criterion `det_ez_ne_zero_of_odd_fiber` (now proved) reduces
Chebotarev's theorem to a purely `mod 2` counting statement, discarding the signs entirely: an odd
fibre of the exponent map already forces the minor to be nonsingular, so no cancellation analysis
of `±1`'s is needed.

**Why now?** The reduction is formalised here, and the resulting statement is a finite parity
question about `Sₙ` acting through a bilinear exponent, amenable to Lucas-type or
Frobenius/`char 2` arguments rather than to the algebraic-number-theoretic machinery that the
signed version demands.

## Conjecture C (Structured-support extension). If `supp f` is contained in the union of two arithmetic progressions of total length `m ≤ p`, then `|supp f̂| ≥ p + 1 − m`.

**The key insight is** that the proof of `card_supp_dft_ge_of_supp_subset_AP` only used that a
function supported on an AP has Fourier transform of the form `ω^{-ka} P(ω^{-kd})` with
`deg P < m`; for a union of two progressions the transform becomes
`ω^{-ka} P(ω^{-kd}) + ω^{-kb} Q(ω^{-ke})`, an exponential polynomial whose zero count is still
governed by a resultant of bounded degree.

**Why now?** This is the smallest genuine strengthening beyond one progression, it needs no new
Mathlib theory (only resultants of two univariate polynomials), and it would already cover all
supports of size ≤ 4 in `ZMod p` for `p ≥ 7`, closing the first open case of Conjecture A by a
different route.

## Conjecture D (Quantitative composite defect). For every `n` with smallest prime factor `q`, `min_{f ≠ 0} (|supp f| + |supp f̂|) = q + n/q`, attained by the indicator of the subgroup of index `q`.

**The key insight is** that the subgroup indicator is simultaneously extremal for the product
bound (`|supp f| · |supp f̂| = n`) and minimal for the sum, so the additive defect of a
composite modulus should be exactly the arithmetic-mean/geometric-mean gap of its factorisation.

**Why now?** `sum_bound_fails_zmod_four` proves the upper bound `q + n/q` for `n = 4`, and the
subgroup computation generalises verbatim; the matching lower bound would be the first
*quantitative* uncertainty principle valid for all moduli, interpolating between Donoho–Stark
and Tao.

## Conjecture E (Learning-theoretic corollary). Over `ZMod p`, any function class of `k`-sparse signals is exactly recoverable from any `p + 1 − k` frequency samples, and this is optimal; consequently sparse recovery on prime cyclic groups needs no incoherence hypothesis.

**The key insight is** that `sum_bound_of_chebotarev_at` is precisely a statement about the
invertibility of arbitrary `k × k` submatrices of the sampling operator, which is the exact
condition for unique `k`-sparse recovery (the "Chebotarev = full spark" phenomenon).

**Why now?** With `chebotarev_iff_sumUncertainty` in place, every increment on Conjectures A–C
transfers automatically into a verified sparse-recovery guarantee; the `|supp f| ≤ 3` case
proved here already yields unconditional recovery of `3`-sparse signals from any `p − 2`
samples.
